public_rationale: A 2024 systematic review documents growing research activity, and the cited Fortune feature describes work across several companies. Together they support the ordinary reading that neurosymbolic AI was gaining attention. They do not establish dominance, widespread deployment or that the trend started that week.
limitations: The result depends on reading vogue as growing attention.
Fortune reports company activity and claims; it does not independently validate their technical performance.
The inspected Fortune text was corrected after the post.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Neurosymbolic AI is finally coming into vogue.

statement.excerpt: Part of the value in skepticism is correctly anticipating road blocks, and suggesting alternative directions (as I have for decades with neurosymbolic AI, which is at last coming into vogue, as noted in Fortune earlier this week).

from_speaker: as noted in Fortune earlier this week
our_interpretation: Coming into vogue means gaining visible research and industry attention, rather than becoming the dominant AI approach.
The current observation is assessed over 2024 through the post, the latest partial calendar year available for research and industry developments.
At last expresses renewed or increasing attention; it does not assert that the field had no previous following.
The assessment concerns the supplied proposition about popularity, not Marcus's separate claim to decades of advocacy.
criteria.support_condition: Research surveys and contemporaneous industry activity show growing attention to neurosymbolic AI, accompanied by visible coverage near the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows declining or stagnant attention, with the cited coverage representing an isolated example rather than a broader trend.
